summary: Added a pure intelligence SubscriptionPool value/state machine alongside the existing ProviderAccountPool routing kernel, then hardened its ADR-0390/0391 proof surface with unit and proptest state-machine coverage. Seats lease as Reserved, complete with typed outcomes, stale/replayed leases are rejected, cooldown/blacklist transitions use existing FailureKind backoff, quota floor is enforced, failure counts reset only on success, and count/unique-lease invariants are asserted across generated operation sequences. The provider-pool app crate now re-exports the pure SubscriptionPool/SeatLease API so composition/proxy lanes can depend on the intelligence app boundary instead of reaching around it; a dedicated app integration test proves the re-exported seam can lease and complete a subscription seat.

F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A pure intelligence SubscriptionPool reconciles ADR-0384/0390 lease semantics with existing ProviderAccountPool without app-layer I/O or stale paths.
rejected_reasons: Legacy Arc<Mutex>/Drop guard brings concurrency mechanics into the pure value kernel too early.
Only extending pick_account would not model Reserved leases or SeatOutcome completion required by ADR-0390.
Stopping at unit tests would leave ADR-0390/0391 proof-layer intent weaker than the existing legacy cloud reference.

findings: Raw OAuth tokens are not represented; seats carry only SecretReference. PoolExhausted is explicit when no eligible seat exists.
Forged/stale leases cannot complete a reserved seat unless the active LeaseId matches the seat state.
Selection is deterministic over BTreeMap seat order with O(n) scan per lease and no heap allocation beyond existing seat-id snapshot vector.
New kernel declaration fields are annotated; full data-class gate is blocked by unrelated cloud-billing baseline.

Additive kernel API plus app re-export seam; removal would be limited to provider-pool kernel Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock/src/tests and app pub-use/test/lint-cleanup lines before downstream proxy integration.
Kernel exposes explicit state/count query methods for future app metrics without adding logging or I/O.
No stale llm-gateway/cloud-intelligence target names were added; ADR-0384 names were treated as historical design-provenance under accepted intelligence ADRs.
Assumption checked: the next foundation build belongs under intelligence; ADR-0335 and specs/microservices/intelligence.json support that placement.
This is the serialization bottleneck before app proxy/OpenBao/SSE work: pure kernel first, proof-hardened kernel second, app composition seam third, then provider transport and admin/console lanes.
The app re-export keeps the intelligence provider-pool kernel usable through the composition crate while preserving ADR-0384 phase-1 constraints: no I/O, no secrets, exhaustively testable.
